doom.driver: Ebola cases surpass 8,000 as DRC struggles to control outbreak. Fatalities near 4,000 across the DRC as health workers battle community anger and a vaccine-resistant strain.
doom.blurb: SOME TROUBLE WITH THE EBOLA VACCINE
doom.summary: Eight thousand Ebola cases, nearly 4,000 dead, a strain that shrugs off the vaccine, and a Congolese politician beaten to death for promoting prevention on the radio. Meanwhile, five men were arrested near an RAF base that launches US bombers against Iran, Trump rejected Tehran's offer to pause the fighting, and Russian drones set Ukraine's Academy of Sciences on fire. Nvidia says it can now catch rogue AI agents within milliseconds, which would be more comforting if OpenAI's agents hadn't spent the summer hammering a UN website 16,000 times.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: AI keeps producing math results, including a never-repeating 3D tiling, while Claude Opus 5.5 and fresh agent tooling ship into a workforce that isn't ready for them.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Florida is asking a court to block ChatGPT while Trump cancels $810 million in congressionally approved spending that some in his own party call illegal.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: The US-Iran war grinds on, with Hormuz attacks, a foiled bomb plot at a UK base hosting US bombers, Russian strikes on Kyiv, and a suspicious blast in the Korean DMZ.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Rogue-agent incidents are now common enough that Nvidia built a product around containing them and legal scholars are debating who is liable.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A vaccine-resistant Ebola strain, a record-breaking El Niño threatening harvests, and Bangkok underwater make a strong case that nature is having a busy week.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — silhouette composition, a lone figure stands in the doorway of a cinderblock home on the outskirts of Butembo, North Kivu, framed by a vivid blood-orange sky bleeding through volcanic haze over distant green hills. The doorway silhouette shows a woman gripping a folded quarantine notice, her small child pressed against her leg, both rendered as pure black shapes against the glowing horizon. Behind them, a dirt path churned to red-brown mud leads toward a distant fenced compound glimpsed only as a low silhouette of tin roofs and a faint MSF flag shape, deliberately blurred by dusk haze. A motorbike lies overturned in the yard, abandoned mid-errand, its wheel still silhouetted against the light. A chlorine jerrican sits untouched by the threshold, and laundry hangs motionless on a line, backlit like ghosts. Cool tones are nearly extinguished — only the deep black foreground shapes and the searing orange-black gradient sky remain, evoking isolation, grief, and a household forever changed by what waits beyond the frame.

dawn.driver: SpaceX's Starship launches on first orbital mission from Texas. Starship is key to SpaceX's commercial success and NASA's plans to land humans on the moon. This is the 14th flight of the uncrewed Starship, but the first time it reached orbit.
dawn.blurb: STARSHIP BREAKS INTO ORBIT AT LAST
dawn.summary: Fourteen flights, a string of fiery setbacks, and then Monday morning the largest rocket ever built reached orbit and splashed down in the Pacific, bringing humans back to the Moon a real step closer. It lands on a heavy day of rogue AI agents, drone strikes on Kyiv and a spiraling Ebola outbreak, and it doesn't erase any of that. Still, alongside ancient proteins revived to fight superbugs and Venezuelan dissidents walking free, it is a reminder that persistence still pays off.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Researchers resurrected 160-million-year-old antimicrobial peptides that outperformed modern human versions against drug-resistant bacteria, while another team traced Alzheimer's damage to immune cells activated outside the brain.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: The US and China agreed to lower tariffs on $60 billion of goods and sent two giant pandas to Atlanta, as Venezuela released dozens of political prisoners.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Shoestring night schools in Lesotho are teaching young herders to read, proof that education finds a way even on the mountainside.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Community push-back helped scrap Sydney's controversial Project Mars data centre, a small win for local voices in the resource fight over AI infrastructure.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A researcher with no academic background in the field used AI to discover a 3D shape that fills all space without ever repeating, an amateur triumph in pure mathematics.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Night scene, all light from artificial sources, deep shadows dominating. The environment is a quiet small-town laundromat after closing hours, rows of dark washing machines lining the walls, a lone television bolted high in the corner casting the only glow across the room. On the screen, a small warm silhouette of a rocket mid-launch glows in golden-orange against a starry TV-static background, reflected faintly on the tile floor below. A folded newspaper sits abandoned on a plastic chair, its front page showing a tiny illustrated rocket icon catching the TV's golden light. Steam drifts faintly from a vending machine humming beside stacked coin-op dryers, its buttons glowing soft green. Moonlight-blue shadows pool in the corners while the television's warm golden flicker washes over dryer lint scattered on the floor and a forgotten mug of coffee on the counter. The overall palette balances confident golden-yellow light against cool green-black shadows, steady and hopeful despite the late hour.
